texts.preamble: (Common Sri Damodara vs ) M/S.Plr Projects Pvt on 29 January, 2020 Scch 1 1 Mvc 3754, 3755 & 3756/2018 In The Court Of The Chief Judge, Court Of Small Causes, Bengaluru & Member, Prl.Mact At Bengaluru
texts.facts: 1 COMMON JUDGMENT 1. These petitions have arisen out of the same accident and therefore, they are taken up together for disposal by this common judgment. 2. MVC No.3754/2018 has been filed by the petitioner seeking compensation of Rs.25 lakhs for the death of his wife Smt.G.Mamatha, MVC No.3755/2018 seeking compensation of Rs.10 lakhs for the death of his son G.Lohith and Mvc No.3756/2018 seeking compensation of Rs.10 lakhs for the injuries suffered by him in the motor vehicle accident which occurred on 13.05.2018 at about 03.45 pm., on NH 42 Road, Kaigal SCCH 1 3 MVC 3754, 3755 & 3756/2018 Village, Baireddipalle Mandal, Chittoor District, Andhra Pradesh. 3. The brief facts of the case are that:- On 13.05.2018, the petitioner as rider with his wife deceased G.Mamatha and his deceased son G.Lohith as pillion riders, was travelling on Motorcycle No.AP.03/B.9407 from Baireddypalle Village towards V.Kota with care and caution on the left side of the road. At about 03.45 pm., when they reached near Kaigal Village on NH 42 Road, Baireddipalle Mandal, Chittoor District, a lorry bearing registration No.AP.03/TD.9390 driven by its driver in rash and negligent manner so as to endanger human life and (Common Sri Damodara vs ) M/S.Plr Projects Pvt on 29 January, 2020 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/187016359/ 2 safety of others came from opposite direction and dashed against their motorcycle. As a result of the terrible impact, petitioner, his wife and son sustained grievous injuries. SCCH 1 4 MVC 3754, 3755 & 3756/2018 4. It is the further case of the petitioner that his wife G.Mamatha succumbed to the injuries at PES Hospital, Kuppam while undergoing treatment. After post mortem, the petitioner has performed the last rites by incurring huge expenses. The deceased was aged 30 years at the time of the accident and working as tailor and earning Rs.15,000/- per month. On account of her untimely death, he has been put to untold hardship and misery and hence, has claimed a compensation of Rs.25 lakhs from the respondents. 5. It is the further case of the petitioner that in the accident, his son G.Lohith sustained grievous injuries and died at the spot. After post mortem, he has performed the last rites. At the time of the accident, his son was aged 7 years. On account of death of his son in the accident, he has suffered severe mental agony and hardship and hence, he has claimed a SCCH 1 5 MVC 3754, 3755 & 3756/2018 compensation of Rs.10 lakhs from the respondents. 6 . The petitioner has further contended that (Common Sri Damodara vs ) M/S.Plr Projects Pvt on 29 January, 2020 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/187016359/ 3 in the accident, he has suffered grievous injuries and was initially shifted to PES Hospital, Kuppam and from there, he was shifted to R.L.Jalapa Hospital, Kolar wherein he took treatment as an inpatient and incurred huge expenses for his treatment. At the time of the accident, he was aged 37 years and doing agriculture and also working as cook and earning Rs.20,000/- per month and contributing the same for the maintenance of the family and due to the injuries sustained in the accident and the resultant disability, he is unable to continue his avocation and thereby has suffered loss of future income and hence, has claimed a compensation of Rs.10 lakhs from the respondents. 7 . The further case of the petitioner is that the accident has occurred due to the rash and negligent SCCH 1 6 MVC 3754, 3755 & 3756/2018 driving of the lorry by its driver and the jurisdictional Police have filed charge sheet against him and the respondent No.1 being the Owner and the respondent No.2 being the Insurer of the same, are liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner in all the cases. 8. In response to the Court notices issued on these claim petitions, the respondent No.1 has not chosen to appear before the Court despite service of notice and hence, he has been placed exparte. The respondent No.2, in all the cases, entered appearance (Common Sri Damodara vs ) M/S.Plr Projects Pvt on 29 January, 2020 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/187016359/ 4 through its advocate and has filed statement of objections. 9. The gist of the contentions taken by the respondent No.2 in all the petitions is that: The Petitions are not maintainable for want of jurisdiction. It is for the petitioner to prove that the accident has occurred due to rash and negligent SCCH 1 7 MVC 3754, 3755 & 3756/2018 driving of the lorry No.AP.03/TD.9390 . It is contended that the petitioner in MVC No.3756/2018 who was riding the motorcycle is guilty of contributory negligence and as such, the petitioner is not entitled to claim compensation from the respondents either jointly or severally. It is for the petitioner to prove that G.Mamatha and G.Lohith died on account of the injuries and the petitioner in MVC No.3756/2018 suffered grievous injuries in the accident. The petitions are bad for non joinder of necessary parties ie., the owner and insurer of the Motorcycle No.AP.03/B.9407. It is for the petitioner and 1st respondent to prove that the lorry No.AP.03/TD.9390 was insured with it as the issuance of insurance policy to the said vehicle is yet to be confirmed. 11. In order to prove his case, the petitioner has examined himself as PW 1. The petitioner has also examined the doctor as PW 2 and produced and got marked in all 19 documents as per Ex.P.1 to P.19. The SCCH 1 10 MVC 3754, 3755 & 3756/2018 respondent No.2 has not examined none nor got marked any documents.
texts.arguments: Without prejudice to the said contentions, the respondent No.2 has contended that it is not aware of the correctness or otherwise of the averments in Column No.1 to 6 of the petition about the age, SCCH 1 8 MVC 3754, 3755 & 3756/2018 (Common Sri Damodara vs ) M/S.Plr Projects Pvt on 29 January, 2020 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/187016359/ 5 avocation and income of the deceased and the injured, amount spent for transportation of dead bodies and cremation etc. The petitioner has to prove his relationship with the deceased. The amount of compensation claimed in all the petitions is without any basis. The 1st respondent has to prove that the driver of the lorry had valid and effective driving licence and the lorry was having valid permit and fitness certificate and has prayed to dismiss all the petitions. 18. On the other hand, though the respondent No.2, has contended that the rider of the motor cycle ie the petitioner has contributed to the accident, but it has not proved the same by examining the driver of the lorry, who would be the right person to speak on the point of contributory negligence. 19. 26 . In so far as addition of income towards loss of future prospects, the Hon'ble Apex Court in National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Pranay Sethi and Ors. reported in 2017 ACJ 2700(SC) has held, " In case, the deceased was self-employed or on a fixed salary, an addition of 40% of the established income should be the warrant where the deceased was below the age of 40 years. An addition of 25% where the deceased was between the age of 40 to 50 years and 10% where the deceased was between the age of 50 to 60 years should be regarded as the necessary method of computation. The established income means the income minus the tax component". In Hemraj Vs. SCCH 1 18 MVC 3754, 3755 & 3756/2018 (Common Sri Damodara vs ) M/S.Plr Projects Pvt on 29 January, 2020 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/187016359/ 12 Oriental Insurance Co. & others reported in (2018) ACJ(5) relied upon by the learned counsel for the petitioners , the Hon'ble Apex Court has held that future prospects is admissible where minimum income is determined on guess work in the absence of proof of income. 27 . In the case on hand, the income of the deceased is taken as Rs.8000/- p.m. In this regard it is useful to the refer to the decision of the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in the case of A.Manavalagan Vs A.Krishnamurthy and others (ILR 2004 KAR 3268 = 2005 ACJ 992). The Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in the said decision while summarizing the principles for SCCH 1 20 MVC 3754, 3755 & 3756/2018 determining the compensation where the claimant is not a dependent has held as follows:- "19. We may summarize the principles enunciated, thus:- (i) xxxxxxx (ii) xxxxxx (iii) Where the claim by the legal representatives of the deceased who were not dependents of the deceased , then the basis for award of compensation is the loss to the estate, that is the loss of savings by the deceased. 30. The Hon'ble Apex Court in National Insurance Company Ltd., Vs Pranay Sethi & others has held that SCCH 1 23 MVC 3754, 3755 & 3756/2018 reasonable figure of Rs.15,000/- towards funeral expenses and Rs.40,000/- towards loss of consortium has to be awarded. the deceased was minor, it is useful to refer to the decision of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of (Common Sri Damodara vs ) M/S.Plr Projects Pvt on 29 January, 2020 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/187016359/ 17 Kishan Gopal and another Vs Lala and others reported in 2013 ACJ 2594, wherein in the said case, the deceased was a minor aged about 10 years and the Hon'ble Apex Court, after considering all the attending facts, awarded Rs.4,50,000/- towards loss of dependency and Rs.50,000/- towards conventional heads and in all, awarded Rs.5,00,000/- as compensation. 43.The petitioner at the age of 45 years has suffered 11% disability to the whole body and he has to lead rest of his life with this disability and discomfort .
